podcast.body: In a 1975 review by Bud Scoppa for the Tampa Tribune, the re-recorded version of "Turn to Stone" was praised for showcasing Walsh's refined style. Scoppa noted that the second performance featured Walsh "playing less, but with more awareness of the power of suggestion," resulting in an "increase in restraint" and "an increase in drama." "The new version shows how well he's honed his style over the past two years. The first performance relied on power recording for impact. The second shows Walsh playing less, but with more awareness of the power of suggestion."

podcast.body: Joe Walsh wrote this song about his deep frustration with the Nixon administration's handling of the Vietnam War and the ongoing protests, fueled by his personal experience at the Kent State shootings. Originally recorded for his 1972 album "Barnstorm," it was re-recorded in 1975 for "So What." The lyrics convey a sense of weariness with political rhetoric: "backyard people and they work all day, tired of the speeches and the way that the reasons keep changing just to make the words rhyme." "Turn to Stone was written about the Nixon administration and the Vietnam War and the protesting that was going on and all of that."
